post_topic: Removing a broken integration entirely instead of patching it
image_description:
Single standalone diagram. One concept only. No panels, no grids, no collages. Full bleed 1080x1080px white background.

A horizontal flow diagram split into two rows labeled 'BEFORE' (top row) and 'AFTER' (bottom row), separated by a clean horizontal dividing line with a downward arrow labeled 'Remove, don't patch' in amber #F5A623.

TOP ROW (BEFORE): Left to right — a box labeled 'Core Product' connected by a solid navy arrow to a box labeled 'Broken Integration' with a red warning icon (⚠) inside it. From 'Broken Integration', dashed navy arrows fan out to five boxes arranged in a loose arc: 'UI Component A', 'UI Component B', 'API Handler', 'State Manager', and 'Config File'. Each dashed arrow is labeled with a small amber callout reading 'dependency'. The overall shape looks tangled and wide. A small amber badge in the top-right of this row reads '10 files touched'.

BOTTOM ROW (AFTER): Left to right — a box labeled 'Core Product' connected by a single solid blue #5a96ff arrow directly to a box labeled 'Clean System Boundary'. No other nodes. No branching arrows. The path is straight and short. A small navy label below the arrow reads 'Smaller. Understood. Owned.'

Diagram title at the top in navy bold text: 'Remove It. Don't Route Around It.'

Navy #0A0F1E primary elements, blue #5a96ff highlights, amber #F5A623 callouts and important labels. Clean sans-serif font. Real cloud provider logos where relevant. Small text 'Kelvin Davis' bottom right corner. Professional LinkedIn infographic style similar to ByteByteGo. White background. No dark backgrounds.
